content:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots; apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast slope by 10–15% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-volatility periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show small price swings, forecast should be anchored closer to 14-day moving average.
- In high-sentiment volatility (sentiment std > 0.3), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth 30d forecast with 7-day exponential decay filter to reduce false peaks.
